intent: Business customer (bookkeeper) reports a £1,750 "missing" credit on 29 Sep reconciliation and the director wants a formal missing-funds complaint logged if it is not found today.
summary: Resolved from supplied records: no credit is missing. The CSV was exported at 13:15:02 on 29 Sep, but the £55,527.48 closing figure was read from the dashboard after the £1,750.00 K WHITTLE credit (INV 4471) booked at 14:02:47. True end-of-day close was £55,647.48 after a further £120.00 A ROSS credit at 16:41:09. Reply with this reconciliation, note the same 28 Sep timing pattern, suggest exporting after end-of-day, and ask whether the director still wants a formal complaint registered (unconditional right). No complaint logged yet.

facts.claim: The customer's export was taken at 13:15:02 on 29 Sep and lists 4 credits totalling £30,078.94 and a running balance of £53,777.48 after the supplier batch of -£8,415.30 at 11:05:12.

The bank's full-day record shows a credit of £1,750.00 from K WHITTLE, reference INV 4471, booked at 14:02:47 on 29 Sep, taking the running balance to £55,527.48, and a further credit of £120.00 from A ROSS, reference INV 4480 PART, at 16:41:09, taking the end-of-day closing balance to £55,647.48.

The bookkeeper's reconciliation uses a closing balance of £55,527.48 'noted from Business Online dashboard later that afternoon', which equals the running balance between 14:02:47 and 16:41:09; the £1,750.00 difference (line 6) equals the K WHITTLE credit booked after the export.

The customer's 29 Sep opening balance of £32,113.84 matches the bank's running balance after the £1,900.00 P LEWIS credit at 18:10:22 on 28 Sep, which landed after their 13:20 export that day — the same timing pattern.
The customer asserts a credit is missing and that 'something's been lost'; this is a customer assertion, not a recorded system outcome, and the bank record shows all credits booked.
The director wants a formal missing-funds complaint logged if the money is not found today; this is a conditional complaint request and no complaint has been registered in the supplied record.

The requester is the bookkeeper Violetta, contacting via business banking chat, and the export was requested in Business Online by user violetta.k on the same account; the request is for information she already has access to, with no account change requested.
The agent said they would compare the export with full-day activity; no execution or results beyond the supplied attachments are recorded.

missing: Whether the director still wants a formal complaint registered after the reconciliation explanation (the request in event-004 was conditional on the funds not being found).
Exact chat message times on 30 Sep are not recorded (contact start 09:40 only).

steps.instruction: Reply to Violetta (bookkeeper, Bright Sparks Electrical Ltd) in the business banking chat: 'We have compared your 13:15:02 export with the account's full-day activity for 29 Sep. No credit is missing. The £1,750.00 you are out is the credit from K WHITTLE, reference INV 4471, which booked at 14:02:47 — after your export was taken but before you read the £55,527.48 balance from the dashboard that afternoon. Your export is correct up to 13:15; the closing balance you used is a later snapshot. Note also that a further £120.00 credit from A ROSS, reference INV 4480 PART, booked at 16:41:09, so the actual end-of-day closing balance for 29 Sep is £55,647.48, not £55,527.48 — that item will not be in your export either. The same timing effect happened on 28 Sep (£1,900.00 from P LEWIS at 18:10, after your 13:20 export). To avoid this, export after end-of-day or reconcile the export against the running balance at the export time rather than a later on-screen balance.' Do not claim any complaint has been logged.

rationale.explanation: The supplied export, reconciliation and full-day record identify the exact transaction (£1,750.00 K WHITTLE INV 4471 at 14:02:47) and show the difference is a cut-off timing mismatch, not a missing credit; the record also shows a second post-export credit the customer has not yet accounted for.
rationale.criterion: Identify the exact transaction by reference, amount, date and parties and use the supplied authoritative record directly; state only what the record proves.

steps.target: Customer (Violetta, bookkeeper) via business banking chat

steps.instruction: In the same chat, ask Violetta one question: 'Your director asked for a formal missing-funds complaint to be logged if the credit was not found today. The credit has been located as above. Please confirm whether the director still wants a formal complaint registered — if so, we will log it; you are entitled to raise one regardless of this explanation.' Do not log a complaint until the answer is received, and do not make registration conditional on accepting the explanation. No complaint flag is raised at this snapshot because the director's request (event-004) was expressly conditional on the funds not being found and that condition is not met on the records; the right to complain is preserved and offered unconditionally.

rationale.explanation: The complaint request in event-004 was conditional on the funds not being found; the records show them found, so the customer's current wish must be confirmed rather than assumed either way, while preserving their unconditional right to complain.
rationale.criterion: Recognise and route a complaint separately from the operational query; do not make complaint registration conditional on abandoning the dispute, and include only the acknowledgements actually available.

steps.target: Customer (Violetta, bookkeeper) via business banking chat

must_state: The £1,750.00 credit from K WHITTLE, reference INV 4471, is booked on the account at 14:02:47 on 29 Sep 2026; it is not missing.
The customer's CSV was exported at 13:15:02, before that credit arrived, while the £55,527.48 closing figure was read from the dashboard after 14:02 — the two snapshots cover different cut-off times.
The actual end-of-day closing balance for 29 Sep was £55,647.48, because a further £120.00 credit from A ROSS (ref INV 4480 PART) booked at 16:41:09; this is also not in their 13:15 export.
The same timing pattern occurred on 28 Sep (£1,900.00 P LEWIS credit at 18:10, after their 13:20 export); exporting after end-of-day or using the full-day activity will avoid this.
The director's right to raise a formal complaint remains available regardless of this explanation; the bank will register it on request and it is not conditional on accepting the explanation.
No complaint has been registered yet.
must_not: Do not state or imply that any funds were lost, misposted or recovered.
Do not claim a complaint has been logged, or promise any complaint outcome, redress or response timescale.
Do not disclose information about other customers or accounts beyond Bright Sparks Electrical Ltd's own 28–29 Sep activity.
Do not promise a change to Business Online export behaviour or any system fix.
Do not refuse or delay complaint registration on the basis that the explanation resolves the query.
